## Graduate Laptop Fit Snapshot

For a graduate student doing programming, writing, and occasional photo editing, the best choice depends on whether you value **portability** or **raw workspace/performance** more. All three fit under the $1,200 ceiling, but they optimize for different priorities.

## Ranked Laptop Comparison

| Rank | Option | Best For | Strengths | Tradeoffs | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A** | Balanced daily use | Strong all-around mix; 16 GB RAM; 512 GB SSD; reasonable weight; solid battery | Not as roomy as B for heavy multitasking; not as light/long-lasting as C | **$1,050** |
| 2 | **C** | Maximum portability | Lightest; longest battery; lowest price | Smallest storage; less comfortable for long coding/photo sessions; weaker fit for larger projects | **$980** |
| 3 | **B** | Performance-first work | Best RAM and storage; larger screen; strongest for multitasking and photo work | Heaviest; shortest battery; closest to budget ceiling | **$1,150** |

## Best Overall Fit by Priority

### If you want the best overall balance
**Buy A.**
It is the most rounded option for a graduate student: enough RAM for programming and multitasking, enough storage for coursework and tools, and a good balance of portability and battery life.

### If portability matters most
**Buy C.**
It is the easiest to carry every day, lasts the longest away from a charger, and costs the least. The main compromise is **256 GB storage**, which may feel tight if you keep many datasets, apps, or photo files locally.

### If performance matters most
**Buy B.**
It is the strongest choice for heavier multitasking, larger photo files, and keeping many apps/tabs open. The tradeoff is that it is the **heaviest** and has the **shortest battery life**.

## Tradeoff Breakdown

- **A vs C:** A gives you more storage and a more balanced setup; C gives you lighter weight and longer battery life.
- **A vs B:** B is clearly better for demanding workloads, but A is more practical if you move around campus a lot.
- **B vs C:** B wins on performance and capacity; C wins on portability and endurance.

## Recommendation

- **Best overall buy:** **A**
- **Choose C** if you carry your laptop all day and want the best battery life.
- **Choose B** if you expect heavier coding, more multitasking, or more frequent photo editing.
